title: Liquid Ring Vacuum Pump
model_title: Liquid Ring Vacuum Pump (Single Stage, Port Plate)

introduction.definition: A liquid ring vacuum pump has an eccentric bladed impeller in a casing partly filled with liquid. The liquid forms a ring; because of the eccentricity the spaces between blades grow (suction) and shrink (compression). It handles wet, dirty and condensable gases.
key_points: Vacuum limited by service-liquid vapour pressure
Cavitation if run below its limit

classification.type: Liquid ring, single stage, flat port plate

introduction.summary: A liquid ring vacuum pump has a bladed impeller mounted off-centre in a round casing partly filled with liquid (usually water). As it turns, the liquid is thrown out to form a ring concentric with the casing. Because the impeller is eccentric, the spaces between blades grow (drawing gas in through the suction port) and then shrink (compressing it out through the discharge port). It tolerates wet, dirty and condensable gases.

steps.text: Rotation throws the service liquid into a ring concentric with the casing.
On the suction side the liquid recedes from the hub and the cells draw gas in through the port plate.
On the other side the liquid moves in, compressing the gas.
Gas and some liquid leave through the discharge port to the separator; liquid is cooled and returned.

foundation: Mount on a rigid, level foundation or grouted baseplate sized for the machine mass and dynamic loads (typically ≥3–5 × machine mass for reciprocating machines).
Check for soft foot before final bolting.
alignment: Align driver and driven shafts with a laser or dial-indicator method to the coupling maker's tolerances; re-check hot alignment where thermal growth is significant.
piping: Provide service-liquid supply with flow control and cooling; discharge separator above the pump.
commissioning: Check rotation direction with the coupling disconnected.
Fill lubricant to the correct level and grade.
Start unloaded where possible; record vibration, temperatures, current and pressures as a baseline.

video_tutorials.title: Liquid Ring Vacuum Pump — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Liquid Ring Vacuum Pump.
A liquid ring vacuum pump has an eccentric bladed impeller in a casing partly filled with liquid.
The liquid forms a ring; because of the eccentricity the spaces between blades grow (suction) and shrink (compression).
It handles wet, dirty and condensable gases.
Typical applications include paper machine vacuum; steam-condenser air removal; chemical process vacuum (solvent recovery); vacuum filtration, priming systems.

The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Casing (eccentric to impeller), Impeller (12 forward-curved blades) & Shaft — eccentric, Port Plate (suction & discharge ports) & Head, Front Head (hidden in cutaway).
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

video_tutorials.title: Liquid Ring Vacuum Pump — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Liquid Ring Vacuum Pump.
Check service-liquid flow and temperature.
Descale casing and port plate.
Inspect impeller for cavitation erosion; replace seals/bearings.
Watch for cavitation: rattling noise, erosion. Common cause: operating below the minimum suction pressure, hot service liquid.
Watch for loss of capacity: higher suction pressure. Common cause: hot or too little service liquid, scale.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
